Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

text.text: Introduction: The introduction of pneumococcal conjugate vaccines resulted in a decline in invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD).
Nevertheless, recent studies report a re-emergence of vaccineincluded serotypes.
Aim: To describe the recent re-emergence of serotype 14 IPD among adults in Catalonia and to investigate the factors underlying its resurgence.

Methods: We analysed two collections of adult IPD isolates: a historical series from Hospital Universitari de Bellvitge (1996Bellvitge ( -2025) )  and a multicentre series from seven tertiary hospitals in Catalonia (2023-2025).
Isolates were serotyped (Quellung) and genotyped by PFGE/MLST  or Illumina sequencing (2023)(2024)(2025).
Clinical data were retrospectively collected.
Results: The historical series showed that, after peaking in 2009, serotype 14 frequency gradually declined, with only 0-4 cases reported annually between 2016 and 2020.
However, the number of serotype 14 isolates increased again in 2025, reaching 11.0% of all isolates at HUB and 10.8% across Catalonia.
Genomic data showed that this increase involved multiple previously circulating lineages (GPSC6, GPSC18, GPSC16 and GPSC39), with no dominant clone.
Analysis of the capsular locus revealed substantial genetic diversity, with no association between capsular variants and either lineage or year of isolation.
A substantial proportion of patients (56.3%) had multiple comorbidities and only 18.8% were appropriately vaccinated.
Discussion: The re-emergence of serotype 14 was not associated with a novel lineage or capsular variant.
Instead, it may reflect a combination of post-pandemic transmission changes, highervalency paediatric vaccines, and natural fluctuations in serotype circulation.
These findings highlight the limits of herd protection and underscore the need to strengthen adult vaccination, particularly among at-risk populations.
Streptococcus pneumoniae remains one of the leading causes of severe infections attributable to vaccine-preventable bacterial pathogens [1].

text.text: After several years of minimal circulation of serotype 14, we observed a marked resurgence of this serotype in Catalonia three years after the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic.
Elucidating the factors driving the re-emergence of a vaccine-covered serotype as a cause of invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) in adults is essential for anticipating future epidemiological shifts.

To address this, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of serotype 14 that integrated (i) an assessment of epidemiological trends (2023-2025) across Catalonia within the framework of a laboratory-based surveillance programme, (ii) an analysis of the temporal dynamics of circulating lineages over a 30-year period at our hospital and (iii) an in-depth genomic characterisation of this serotype.

This laboratory-based study analysed serotype 14 isolates causing IPD in adults (≥18 years), with IPD defined as the isolation of S. pneumoniae from a normally sterile site in a patient presenting with signs and symptoms of infection.

Clinical data of patients with IPD due to serotype 14 were collected, including demographics, clinical presentation, comorbidities, 30-day mortality and pneumococcal vaccination history from clinical records.
To address the three main objectives, two study collections were established.
The first is a historical collection (C1) that comprised all pneumococcal isolates recovered between 1996 and 2025 at the Microbiology Department of Hospital Universitari de Bellvitge (HUB).

The second is a multicentre collection that (C2) encompassed isolates from seven tertiary care hospitals across Catalonia (2023-2025), representing all four provinces: Barcelona (Hospital Universitari de Bellvitge, Hospital Universitari Germans Trias i Pujol, and Hospital Universitari Vall d'Hebron), Girona (Hospital Universitari Dr.
Josep Trueta), Lleida (Hospital Universitari Arnau de Vilanova), and Tarragona (Hospital Universitari Joan XXIII and Hospital Universitari Verge de la Cinta).
For genomic analysis propose, Genomic Sets (GS) were stablished including strains form C1 and C2 as well closed genomes form public databases.

text.text: Focusing on PCV7 serotypes, their proportion declined progressively from 43.4% in 1996 to 8.5% in 2019.
However, a marked increase was observed in 2025, when they accounted for 17.6% of IPD episodes.
Overall, serotype 14 represented 5.9% of cases (n=155), although its proportion varied substantially during the study period, declining from 13.2% in 1996 to 0.0% in 2016.
The 2025 rise in PCV7 serotypes was largely driven by serotype 14, which accounted for 11.0% of all IPD episodes (Figure 1).

text.text: Focusing on the genetic lineages of serotype 14, GPSC6 was the predominant lineage throughout the study period, accounting for 77.4% of isolates.

Nevertheless, several other lineages were identified, including GPSC18 (13.5%), GPSC16 (1.9%), and GPSC39 (1.9%), together with additional minor lineages, highlighting the genetic heterogeneity of this serotype.
GPSC18 reached its highest prevalence in 1997, exceeding that of GPSC6 (62.5% vs 25.0%), but declined, remaining at low levels until it disappeared after 2011.
Notably, GPSC18 isolates were detected again in 2025, indicating the re-emergence of this historical lineage (Figure 2).

text.text: As part of the Catalan IPD surveillance programme, a total of 1,231 adult IPD episodes were collected across different geographical regions of Catalonia: 399 in 2023, 397 in 2024, and 435 in 2025.
Serotype 14, as observed at HUB, increased in frequency from 0.75% (n=3) in 2023 to 2.5% (n=10) in 2024 and 10.8% (n=45) in 2025 (Figure 3A).

text.text: Among patients with IPD caused by serotype 14 with available clinical data (n=48), the mean age was 62.8 years, and 56.3% of patients were female.
The main clinical presentation was pneumonia, accounting for 83.3% of cases, while meningitis represented 6.3%.
Overall, 56.3% of patients presented one or more comorbidities, with malignancies being the most frequent (22.9%).
The 29.2% of patients presented sepsis and 18.8% were admitted to the ICU.
The 30-day mortality rate was 8.3%.
Among the 48 patients, only a small proportion (18.8%) had been appropriately vaccinated.
Of them, 10.4% had received PCV20, 4.2% PCV13, and 4.2% PPV23 (Table 1).

The most frequently reported conditions were malignancy and immunosuppressive therapy (4/9 patients each).

text.text: WGS analysis identified four distinct serotype 14 lineages associated with IPD in Catalonia, all of which had previously been detected in the HUB collection.
GPSC6 was the most prevalent lineage, accounting for five cases in 2024 and 26 cases in 2025.
This lineage exhibited substantial genetic diversity and comprised several sequence types (STs), including ST143, ST156, ST1227, and six additional minor STs.
GPSC18 accounted for one case in 2023, 3 in 2024, and 6 in 2025, all of them ST9 or ST409.
All isolates of GPSC39 were ST124 (1 in 2024 and 5 in 2025) and a single case of GPSC16 (ST67) was detected in 2025 (Figure 3B).

text.text: GPSC6 presented the highest diversity, with many PBP profiles and differences in antibiotic resistance mechanisms.
ST156 was resistant to penicillin and amoxicillin and non-susceptible to cefotaxime; in addition, the I100L substitution in DHFR conferred resistance to cotrimoxazole.
The same β-lactam resistance profile was shown by ST143, which also harboured the erm(B) gene, conferring resistance to macrolides and clindamycin.
ST1227 carried both erm(B) and the aph(3')-IIIa gene, the latter conferring resistance to aminoglycosides.
Both STs of GPSC18 were susceptible to βlactams and shared the same PBP profile, but ST9 genomes carried the mef(A) gene, conferring resistance to macrolides.
The single GPSC16 (ST67) strain was resistant to penicillin and amoxicillin.
Strains of ST124 (GPSC39) were fully susceptible to antibiotics, without any acquired resistance genes in their genomes.

text.text: The capsular operon is the main virulence factor of pneumococcus.

The capsular biosynthetic locus of serotype 14 includes 4 regulatory genes (wzg, wzh, wzd and wze), the initial transferase (wchA), the polymerase (wzy), the flippase (wzx) and seven glycosyl transferases (wchJ, wchK, wchL, wchM, wchN, wchY and lrp).
The lrp gene encodes for a large repetitive protein that could serves as a dominant antigen [20].

text.text: Catalonia has long-established paediatric immunisation programme, in which PCV13 achieved an uptake above 94% between 2017 and 2022.
Since 2023, children have been vaccinated with PCV15, with coverage exceeding 96%.
However, the landscape of adult vaccination differs considerably.
According to the official Spanish report, PPV23 uptake reached 40.1% in 2021, whereas PCV20, introduced in our region in November 2022, achieved a coverage of 26.1% by 2025 [21].

text.text: Given this limited adult coverage, the substantial decline in the incidence of PCV13 serotypes in adults, with the exception of serotype 3, is probably attributable to the indirect protection conferred by routine childhood PCV13 vaccination [22].

In England, an increase in serotype 4 has been linked to the emergence of a novel lineage, and similar trends have been observed in Spain [8, 23].

text.text: In this manuscript, we describe the re-emergence of serotype 14 a cause of IPD among adults in Catalonia after the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic.
Several hypotheses could explain the observed upsurge 25 years after the introduction of PCV7 into childhood vaccination.
The expansion of new lineages may have contributed to this resurgence.
However, our results showed that this increase was driven by multiple genetically distinct lineages, the clonal expansion of a single lineage is unlikely to fully explain this phenomenon.
In fact, the rise of serotype 14 in our study was primarily associated with lineages that had been predominant in Spain prior to the introduction of PCVs [4, 12].
text.formatted: In fact, the rise of serotype 14 in our study was primarily associated with lineages that had been predominant in Spain prior to the introduction of PCVs <ref type="bibr" target="#b3">[4,</ref> <ref type="bibr">12]</ref>.

text.text: The emergence of a capsular variant capable of evading vaccine-induced immunity may also have played a role in this upsurge.
Expansion of serotype 14 following the implementation of PCV13 vaccination programmes was previously reported and attributed to the emergence of novel variants with altered capsular structures [25].
text.formatted: Expansion of serotype 14 following the implementation of PCV13 vaccination programmes was previously reported and attributed to the emergence of novel variants with altered capsular structures <ref type="bibr" target="#b22">[25]</ref>.

text.text: Molecular analyses have revealed diversity within the capsular operon, including truncation of wciY and variation in lrp.
Our data indicate that substantial variation exists in the number of repeats within the lrp locus [26].
text.formatted: Our data indicate that substantial variation exists in the number of repeats within the lrp locus <ref type="bibr" target="#b23">[26]</ref>.

text.text: However, the biological significance of these capsular operon variations remains unclear, and their impact beyond genomic characterization has yet to be determined.
Taken together, these findings argue against an exclusive role of a newly emerged vaccine-escape capsule in driving the observed expansion.

Similary, the presence of a diverse genetic background suggests that the resurgence is unlikely to be driven by the acquisition of unknown non-capsular genetic determinants that selectively favoured the expansion of serotype 14 lineages.

One of the characteristics of PCVs is their ability to prevent nasopharyngeal colonisation, a prerequisite for disease development, and to induce serotype-specific memory B cells, thereby conferring long-term protection.
However, weaker memory responses have been described for some serotypes, which could lead to a shorter period of protection [7].
text.formatted: However, weaker memory responses have been described for some serotypes, which could lead to a shorter period of protection <ref type="bibr" target="#b6">[7]</ref>.

text.text: Protection against colonisation and disease correlates with the levels of functional antibodies induced, with substantially higher antibody concentrations required to prevent colonisation than to protect against invasive disease.
Compared with other pneumococcal serotypes, serotype 14 has been shown to require higher antibody concentrations to achieve protection against colonisation [27].
text.formatted: Compared with other pneumococcal serotypes, serotype 14 has been shown to require higher antibody concentrations to achieve protection against colonisation <ref type="bibr" target="#b24">[27]</ref>.

text.text: Furthermore, newer higher-valency conjugate vaccines have demonstrated reduced immunogenicity for serotypes shared with earlier formulations, such as PCV7 and PCV13, potentially increasing the risk of pneumococcal colonisation as predicted by modelling studies [28].

text.text: As PCV15 replaced PCV13 in the paediatric vaccination programme in Catalonia in 2023, changes in the magnitude or persistence of serotype 14-specific antibody responses could have affected the ability of the vaccine to reduce carriage of this serotype in children, potentially facilitating its transmission to adults [29].

text.text: However, we have not data on the impact of these new PCVs colonisation in children.
Furthermore, serotype 14 IPD episodes occurred mostly in unvaccinated adults.

The few cases identified among vaccinated individuals were largely confined to high-risk patients, including those with immunosuppression or severe underlying comorbidities who recovered after successful therapy.
On the other hand, the role of adults in transmission has been increasingly recognised as important for the maintenance of most PCV serotypes [30].
text.formatted: On the other hand, the role of adults in transmission has been increasingly recognised as important for the maintenance of most PCV serotypes <ref type="bibr" target="#b28">[30]</ref>.

text.text: With the recent changes in the epidemiology after the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, the resurgence of different respiratory diseases makes it plausible that adults act as transmitters of vaccine serotypes.
These findings suggest that the observed increase in serotype 14 incidence is unlikely to be attributable to changes in vaccination policies within the adult population.

The incidence of highly prevalent serotypes has classically been described as exhibiting fluctuating patterns [31, 32], although PCV introduction has driven faster and larger shifts in serotype prevalence than those attributable to natural fluctuations [33].

text.text: Current pneumococcal serotype dynamics are likely shaped by the interplay between ecological factors, such as competition for the nasopharyngeal niche and naturally acquired population immunity, and the selective pressure exerted by vaccination [7].

text.text: In this context, it is important to note that the re-emergence of serotype 14 occurred immediately after the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, a period that was associated with a marked global decline in the incidence of IPD due to the widespread implementation of non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) [34].

text.text: Reduced interpersonal contact during the pandemic may have limited population-level exposure to pneumococcal serotypes, potentially resulting in a global decline in natural protective immunity, consistent with the concept of an immunity gap [35].

text.text: It is therefore plausible that NPIs, as well as their subsequent lifting, had differential impacts on the circulation and transmission of distinct pneumococcal serotypes.
In this context, the expansion of serotype 14, which requires higher antibody levels to prevent colonisation, may have been favoured.
This study has several notable strengths.
First, the collection spans a long period, allowing the analysis of serotype distribution and lineage dynamics over time.

Second, an in-depth genomic analysis was performed within each lineage, allowing detailed characterisation of sequence types, antibiotic resistance determinants, and capsular locus variability, and providing valuable insight into the molecular epidemiology of serotype 14, including its genetic diversity and evolution over time.
Several limitations should also be acknowledged.

Although the multicentre collection included seven hospitals, it did not cover the entire Catalan region, which has approximately 8 million inhabitants, potentially limiting the generalisability of the findings.

Additionally, the study focused exclusively on adults, characterising serotype 14 dynamics among children would also be highly relevant, given that transmission patterns may differ between age groups.

Furthermore, clinical data were not available for patients with IPD caused by non-serotype 14 pneumococci, limiting our ability to identify potential serotype-specific differences in clinical presentation and outcomes.
In conclusion, different factors, or a combination of them, may have contributed to the reemergence of serotype 14 in adults in our setting.
Notably, vaccination coverage among adults remains low, which is particularly concerning in a population with increasing life expectancy and a growing number of comorbidities.

Further studies are warranted to monitor the evolving dynamics of serotype 14 and other PCV serotypes as vaccination coverage increases.    507 year of isolation, GPSC, ST, MIC for penicillin, amoxicillin, and cefotaxime, PBP1A, 2B, and 2X alleles, acquired 508 resistance genes, and the I100L amino acid substitution in DHFR.

During the study period, 2,631 adult IPD episodes were recorded at HUB.
From 1996 onwards, the annual number of IPD episodes increased progressively, reaching a peak of 147 episodes in 2009.
After the introduction of PCV13, the number of IPD episodes markedly declined to 75 episodes in 2011 and remained stable with occasional fluctuations until 2019.
